value.rationale: The natural question is how much of a randomly inscribed polygon’s area fluctuations are predictable using only its perimeter. The exact unique optimal linear slope and residual variance quantitatively separate predictable cubic spacing fluctuations from irreducible quintic fluctuations; a 33/113 residual variance ratio and n^-4 correlation deficit are genuine joint-shape information not provided by known individual asymptotic laws or the fixed-slope extrapolation. The result can be used as a sharp baseline for multivariate polygonal approximation and variance reduction, without asserting nonlinear optimality.
